editorial:
Imagine being stuck inside during a global lockdown and feeling completely alone. That is where you meet Bernardo and Luix. They are two strangers who find each other through a screen and start a relationship based entirely on talking and dreaming. The vibe is very intimate and quiet, focusing on how people try to connect when they cannot even touch. You will feel the tension as they push the boundaries of their digital romance, trying to find new ways to feel close while the world outside is in total chaos.

What really makes this work is the acting. The two leads make you believe they are falling in love even though they are just talking to a camera. The pacing is slow, which might bore some of you, but it helps you feel the longing they are going through. If you enjoy stories about lonely hearts and modern love, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small facial expressions, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the two characters finally meeting in person after their long time apart. The tension builds up as they move from the digital world to the physical world. You see them realize that their emotional bond is even stronger in real life than it was over video calls. They embrace and accept their feelings, showing that true love can survive even the strangest circumstances and the hardest distance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about long distance relationships and deep conversations.
